chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him). He said: I asked him, 'Is the testimony of women permissible in marriage, or divorce, or in stoning?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of women is permissible in what men are unable to look at, and there is no man with them; and their testimony is permissible in marriage if there is a man with them; and their testimony is permissible in the legal penalty (hadd) of adultery if there are three men and two women; but the testimony of two men and four women is not permissible in adultery and stoning; and their testimony is not permissible in divorce, nor in blood (diya (blood money).'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for the validity of women's testimony in marriage, adultery, and divorce according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details Imam al-Rida’s (AS) nuanced juristic distinctions regarding women's testimony, reflecting the Shia school's adherence to the Quranic principle of 'two women for one man' in specific contexts while allowing for flexibility based on the nature of the evidence. It clarifies that while women cannot testify alone in divorce or blood money (diya), their testimony is valid in marriage and hadd penalties when combined with men, highlighting the practical application of Quranic verses in classical fiqh. The ruling underscores the scholarly view that the requirement for male witnesses is not absolute but contingent upon the specific legal domain and the ability to verify the facts.
